prompts.text: Name a French or British food

items.quip: Some clangers held savoury filling at one end, jam at the other.
items.title: Bedfordshire clanger
items.extract: The Bedfordshire clanger is a dish from Bedfordshire and adjacent counties in England, including Buckinghamshire and Hertfordshire. It dates back to at least the 19th century.

prompts.text: Name something you can measure about the human body

items.quip: Your back can't tell two pinpricks apart closer than about 3 cm.
items.title: Two-point discrimination
items.description: Ability to discern between single and pairs of points on one's skin
items.extract: Two-point discrimination (2PD) is the ability to discern that two nearby objects touching the skin are truly two distinct points, not one. It is often tested with two sharp points during a neurological examination and is assumed to reflect how finely innervated an area of skin is.

items.quip: Monastery schools used it around 1030 to teach Boethius's number theory.
items.title: Rithmomachia
items.extract: Rithmomachia is an early European mathematical board game. Its earliest known description dates from the eleventh century. The name comes loosely from Greek and means "The Battle of the Numbers." The game is somewhat like chess except that most methods of capture depend on the numbers inscribed on each piece.

prompts.text: Name an animal with a one-word name containing "ck"

items.quip: Named for its buzzy song, often written dick-dick-ciss-ciss-ciss.
items.title: Dickcissel
items.extract: The dickcissel is a small seed-eating migratory bird in the family Cardinalidae. It breeds on the prairie grasslands of the Midwestern United States and winters in Central America, northern Colombia, and northern Venezuela. It is the only member of the genus Spiza, though some sources list another supposedly extinct species.

prompts.text: Name a country where another religion has more followers than Christianity

items.quip: Only African country where Hinduism is the largest religion.
items.title: Mauritius
items.description: Island country in the Indian Ocean
items.extract: Mauritius, officially the Republic of Mauritius, is an island country in the Indian Ocean, located about 1,100 nautical miles off the southeastern coast of Africa, east of Madagascar. It includes the main island, as well as Rodrigues, Agaléga, and St. Brandon. The islands of Mauritius and Rodrigues, along with nearby Réunion, are part of the Mascarene Islands. The main island of Mauritius, where the population is concentrated, hosts the capital and largest city, Port Louis. The country spans 2,040 square kilometres (790 sq mi) and has an exclusive economic zone covering approximately 580,000 square nautical miles.

items.title: Nate Ebner
items.description: American football and rugby sevens player (born 1988)
items.extract: Nathan Ebner is an American former professional football player who was a safety and special teamer in the National Football League (NFL). He was a rugby sevens player for the United States national rugby sevens team.

prompts.text: Name a hair type, texture, or natural color

items.quip: Venetian master Titian's red-haired women gave this brownish-orange shade its name.
items.title: Titian
items.extract: Tiziano Vecellio, Latinized as Titianus, hence known in English as Titian, was an Italian Renaissance painter. The most important artist of Renaissance Venetian painting, he was born in Pieve di Cadore, near Belluno.
